Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Law No. 8 of 2014 establishes that National ID Numbers are 'granted at birth, based on an individual's data in the Civil Registry at the Civil Status Authority'. This means enrollment eligibility begins at birth, placing Libya in the lowest age category (0). All Libyan citizens regardless of age receive a NIN upon birth registration. The physical ID card is issued subsequently and is required for adults to access services.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Enrollment is mandatory. Law No. 8 of 2014 establishes that 'No state body may issue any document or service until an individual obtains a national ID number' and the NIN is 'a basic condition for the right to certificates and documents indicative of citizenship and to obtain any public services'. All government ministries and bodies must use the NIN for all administrative, financial, and economic procedures. Salaries are suspended for citizens who do not provide their NIN. Civil Registration Act No. 36 of 1968 makes birth registration obligatory. Failure to comply with identity number requirements is subject to criminal penalties under Law No. 8 of 2014.
